exposure: Fetal Region-specific Optimized Growth Standard (FROGS) classification (<10th centile)
Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW) chart classification (<10th centile)
Mikolajczyk's global fetal and birthweight centile chart classification (<10th centile)
INTERGROWTH-21st fetal growth standards classification (<10th centile)
outcome: operative (instrumental) vaginal birth for suspected fetal compromise
cohort: The cohort consisted of infants classified as small for gestational age (<10th centile) by various growth charts, allowing for comparison of adverse perinatal outcomes between different classification methods.
finding: The Fetal Region-specific Optimized Growth Standard (FROGS) chart outperformed other existing charts, classifying a similar proportion of infants as small for gestational age, in identifying small infants at increased risk of stillbirth and other serious perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: FROGS was better at identifying infants at risk of operative (instrumental) vaginal birth for suspected fetal compromise compared to other charts.
birth_weight: Infants classified as small for gestational age (<10th centile) and <3rd centile were included, and the study retrospectively assessed birthweight.
gest_age: Infants classified as small for gestational age (<10th centile) were included, and the study considered babies born at term for local population adjustments in FROGS.
